chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara and Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who had a slave, so a jeweller or someone else hired him from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he were to waste something or abscond from him, then his masters are responsible.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: Who is liable for a hired slave's loss or absconding according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reflects the judicial precedent of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) regarding *diya* and liability in employment contracts, establishing that the owner bears the risk of loss or absconding (*firaar*) when a slave is hired out. It highlights the principle of *daman* (guarantee) in Shia jurisprudence, where the owner remains liable for the slave's actions or status while in the hirer's custody, ensuring clarity in commercial transactions. This hadith is frequently cited in discussions of *fiqh al-mu'amalat* to define the boundaries of responsibility between employers and owners of hired labor.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara and Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man who had a slave of his, so he was hired from him by a jeweller or someone else’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he were to waste something or abscond from him, so his masters are responsible’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn Muskan from Zurarah and abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ‘Amir al-Mu’minin, issued judgment in favor of a man whose slave was hired by a goldsmith or another man. The judgment said, ‘If he has caused certain damage or has run away with something, the masters are held responsible. 5 ”
